text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croat member of the collective Bosnian Presidency Kresimir Zubak urges presidency's Moslem chairman Alija Izetbegovic, who is on sick leave, to allow an acting chairman to serve in his absence.

- Moslem co-chairman in the Bosnian Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdzic, criticizes international High Representative Carl Bildt for proposals which he said would divide Bosnia's economy between Serb and Moslem-Croat regions.
- President of International Comittee of the Red Cross (ICRC), Cornello Sommaruga, says during Bosnia tour the number of missing from war is estimated to be more than 18,000.
- A manager of the South Korean Daewoo corporation says in Sarajevo his company does not intend to compete with Volkswagen in Bosnia but wants to cooperate with local car industry.
- Russia, Britain and France as members of the international Contact Group are supporting option that gives northern port of Brcko to Bosnian Serbs, the daily quotes diplomats as saying.
- If unjust solution is delivered over town of Brcko, nobody will be able to control situation, Moslem nationalist Party of Democratic Action (SDA) spokesman Ismet Grbo says.
- Another Moslem woman was expelled from her apartment in the Croat controlled part of the divided Bosnian town of Mostar, U.N. police monitor spokesman says.
- Unidentifed assailants hijacked vehicle belonging to Moslem and beat him on road that passes through Bosnian Serb territory on Wednesday, U.N. police monitors report.
